context:
Treat benchmark and platform pages as one browse system. Reuse Home
leaderboard semantics for heatmap, badges, units, and missing values. Add
browse-specific guardrails for cross-benchmark, cross-scale, and sparse trend
interpretation. Keep the pages dense, but make comparability boundaries
visible.
description:
PR #246 captured benchmark and platform browse issues after the route matrix
rendered cleanly: compare selection is too implicit, platform trends have
weak value when data is sparse, platform tables mix benchmark/scale cohorts
without enough guardrails, and the Star Schema route displays SSB naming with
many `0 ms` values that need explicit interpretation.

This TODO turns those browse-page findings into a concrete plan for
BenchmarkIndex, PlatformIndex, QueryHeatmap, trend sections, compare entry,
and benchmark-specific data labels.

anti_patterns.dont: chart mixed benchmark/scale cohorts as a single comparable trend.
display rounded sub-ms values as `0 ms` without an explanation or alternative format.
hide compare entry until after users already know to select rows.
make mobile users inspect large matrices without a scroll cue, sticky context, or card fallback.
make trust and validation badges visually dominate per-query timings.

preserves.behavior: Existing row-selection to Compare flow and compact IDs where available.
Sortable table behavior and receipt/detail links.

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run test:e2e:fixtures && npm run build && npx playwright test --project=chromium --grep "benchmark|platform"
verifications.expected: Chromium browser smoke passes for benchmark and platform routes

verifications.command: echo 'Manual: recapture benchmark and platform routes at 390, 768, 1280, 1600 plus TPC-H list/high-contrast and compare against PR #246 screenshots'
verifications.description: Manual PR #246 browse recapture is clean
verifications.expected: manual evidence shows U-3, DQ-5, and DQ-7 resolved or explicitly deferred

work_units.notes:
Use the PR #246 screenshots to confirm current ownership and behavior in
`BenchmarkIndex.tsx`, `PlatformIndex.tsx`, `QueryHeatmap.tsx`,
`RankTable.tsx`, and trend/sparkline components. Confirm which routes
have one-row cohorts, sparse trends, hidden compare actions, and mobile
overflow.
work_units.summary: Reproduce benchmark and platform browse evidence after current data loads

work_units.notes:
Benchmark and platform pages should show a persistent compare affordance,
disabled state, or selected-result tray that explains the rule before the
user knows to click checkboxes. Single selection should say that two or
more comparable results are required. Incompatible selection should
explain which dimension differs.

Keep the selected-result language and route to Compare consistent across
benchmark and platform pages.
work_units.summary: Make compare selection visible before users select rows
Retheme benchmark matrix/list views around metric and badge clarity

work_units.notes:
The platform table mixes benchmark families, scale factors, phases, and
dates. Group or label rows so users do not read SSB, TPC-H SF0.01, and
TPC-H SF0.1 as one comparable leaderboard. Primary metric labels should
explain whether the value is a power score, geomean latency, or another
benchmark-derived metric.
work_units.summary: Guard platform tables against invalid cross-cohort interpretation

work_units.notes:
For one or two observations, avoid large empty time-series plots that
imply a meaningful trend. Use a compact sparse-data state, sparkline with
explicit "limited observations" label, or hide the trend until enough
points exist. Trend sections must name benchmark, scale, phase, metric,
and unit.
work_units.summary: Replace low-information sparse trends with guarded sparse-data states

work_units.notes:
The `/results/star_schema/` route may use `SSB` as the human-facing label,
but the page must make the Star Schema Benchmark/SSB equivalence explicit.
Values shown as `0 ms` need a formatting rule and visible explanation:
use `<1 ms`, a precision footnote, or another non-misleading display if
values are rounded below precision.
work_units.summary: Clarify Star Schema, SSB naming, and zero/sub-ms timing display

work_units.notes:
Ensure no-result, filtered-empty, one-platform, no-run, and not-comparable
states are actionable. A one-row benchmark matrix or sparse platform
history should tell users what can and cannot be inferred.
work_units.summary: Polish browse empty, filtered-empty, and no-comparison states

work_units.notes:
Add targeted tests for compare affordance, benchmark labels, zero/sub-ms
display, platform grouping, sparse trends, and mobile overflow. Recapture
benchmark and platform screenshots at 390px, 768px, 1280px, and 1600px,
including TPC-H list/high-contrast and Star Schema/SSB routes.
work_units.summary: Add browse-page tests and recapture PR #246 route evidence
